meta.disclaimer: Curated editorial reference compiled from public sources (CSIS Missile Threat, IISS, Wikipedia, DIA, press reporting). Specifications for these systems are approximate and sources frequently disagree; ranges and warhead figures give the commonly cited envelope. Not derived from the alert dataset.

systems.name: Qassam family
systems.origin: Locally improvised in Gaza by Hamas's al-Qassam Brigades (first built 2001)
systems.warhead_notes: Improvised HE (scavenged TNT / urea-nitrate fertilizer mixes) packed with shrapnel; earliest Qassam-1 carried under 1 kg, typical later rounds 5-10 kg, Qassam-3 up to ~20 kg.
systems.speed: Brief solid boost then ballistic; at Sderot ranges residents get roughly 15 seconds of warning
systems.first_used_vs_israel: 2001 (first launches; first deep hit on Sderot 2002)
systems.salvo_notes: October 7, 2023: 2,200-5,000 rockets (largely Qassam/Grad types plus mortars) fired from Gaza in the opening ~20-30 minutes — the largest rocket barrage ever fired at Israel.
systems.notes: The archetypal Gaza rocket: made in workshops from pipe steel and fertilizer, wildly inaccurate but launched in enormous numbers. Its sub-$1,000 cost against ~$50,000 Iron Dome interceptors is the classic cost-asymmetry example.

systems.name: 122mm Grad
systems.origin: Soviet BM-21 design; supplied via Iran and other sources, plus local Gaza-made copies
systems.warhead_notes: HE-fragmentation; standard rounds ~18-21 kg, extended-range and Hezbollah variants documented up to ~30 kg.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Katyusha fire from Lebanon since the 1970s; Grad-type fire from Gaza documented from 2006-2008
systems.salvo_notes: 2006 Lebanon war: Hezbollah fired 3,970-4,228 rockets in 34 days, ~95% of them 122mm Katyushas. November 24, 2024: ~250 projectiles from Lebanon in one day. The workhorse of Gaza barrages incl. May 2021 (4,360 rockets in 11 days).
systems.notes: The single most-fired weapon family behind Israel's red-alert sirens across every front — Hamas, PIJ and Hezbollah all use the same Soviet-designed 122mm round.

systems.name: Mortars (60/81/120mm)
systems.origin: Various — smuggled Iranian/Soviet-pattern and locally produced in Gaza
systems.warhead_notes: Standard HE-fragmentation mortar bombs; a 120mm bomb weighs ~13-16 kg with a few kg of explosive fill.
systems.speed: Low, steep ballistic arc — flight times of seconds give almost no warning near the fence
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Early 2000s (Second Intifada, from Gaza)
systems.salvo_notes: October 7, 2023: IDF counted ~3,000 rockets and mortar bombs fired in the first four hours; mortars blanketed Gaza-envelope communities throughout the war.
systems.notes: The shortest-range threat in the dataset: too fast and low for many Iron Dome engagements close to the fence, mortars caused a large share of casualties in Gaza-border communities in 2014 and 2023.

systems.name: M-75
systems.origin: Gaza-produced copy of Iran's Fajr-5, built in local workshops from Iranian-supplied drawings
systems.warhead_notes: Fajr-5-class HE warhead; exact weight not reliably documented.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: November 2012 (Operation Pillar of Defense — first rockets to reach Tel Aviv and Jerusalem)
systems.salvo_notes: Fired at Tel Aviv/Jerusalem in small numbers in Nov 2012; mass-employed alongside J-80/R-160-class rockets in 2014, May 2021 and from October 7, 2023.
systems.notes: The M-75 marked Hamas's leap from border-area rockets to holding metropolitan Tel Aviv at risk with an indigenized Iranian design. Hamas even released a perfume called 'M75' to celebrate it.

systems.name: Fajr-5
systems.origin: Iran (333mm heavy artillery rocket); smuggled to Gaza, also held in bulk by Hezbollah
systems.warhead_notes: HE-fragmentation; CSIS lists a 90 kg HE warhead, other references cite up to 175 kg — sources disagree.
systems.guidance: unguided (a later Iranian Fajr-5C variant adds satnav guidance)
systems.speed: Supersonic heavy artillery rocket (~915 kg launch weight)
systems.first_used_vs_israel: November 15, 2012 (Hamas/PIJ launches at Tel Aviv)
systems.salvo_notes: Fired in ones and twos at Tel Aviv in Nov 2012; Hezbollah holds thousands of Fajr-3/Fajr-5s as the mid-range tier of its arsenal.
systems.notes: Iran's signature proxy rocket: the transfer of Fajr-5s to both Hezbollah and Gaza was the first big step in extending proxy reach from border towns to Israel's population centers.

systems.name: R-160
systems.origin: Chinese WS-1 design produced in Syria as M-302; smuggled to Gaza, also in Hezbollah stocks as Khaibar-1
systems.warhead_notes: HE-fragmentation; M-302 variants carry ~100-175 kg depending on version.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: July 2014 (Operation Protective Edge — fired toward the Haifa area)
systems.salvo_notes: July 2014: the deepest Gaza strikes to that date (~116 km); the Iranian arms ship Klos-C, seized in March 2014, carried 40 M-302s bound for Gaza. Hezbollah's Khaibar-1 version hit Afula in 2006.
systems.notes: Its 2014 debut forced alert coverage as far north as Haifa and showed Syrian-produced heavy rockets had reached Gaza by sea.

systems.name: Ayyash-250
systems.origin: Hamas-produced (assessed as an Iranian Zelzal-generation design built in Gaza)
systems.warhead_notes: Heavy HE warhead of undocumented weight; accuracy very poor at full range.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: May 2021 (single launch toward Ramon Airport, ~220 km)
systems.salvo_notes: Fired singly: one at Ramon Airport in May 2021; small numbers launched again after October 7, 2023 toward deep targets.
systems.notes: Longest-range weapon known in Hamas's arsenal, named for bombmaker Yahya Ayyash. Its 250 km claim puts essentially all of Israel inside Gaza rocket range on paper.

systems.name: Badr-3
systems.origin: Iranian-designed; primary user is Palestinian Islamic Jihad's al-Quds Brigades
systems.warhead_notes: Very heavy HE warhead for a Gaza rocket — 250 kg of explosive per PIJ, 300-400 kg total per analyst Fabian Hinz; airbursts ~20 m up for wide fragmentation. Range claims disagree sharply: ~13 km as verified in use, 150-160 km claimed.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: May 5, 2019 (PIJ launches at the Ashkelon area)
systems.salvo_notes: Debuted during the ~700-rocket May 2019 escalation; fired again in the May 2021 war and 2022-23 Gaza rounds; IDF captured Badr-3 stocks inside Gaza in 2024.
systems.notes: PIJ's showcase Iranian-designed heavy rocket — what it lacks in range and accuracy it makes up in warhead mass, several times heavier than typical Palestinian rockets.

systems.name: Fajr-3
systems.origin: Iran (240mm heavy artillery rocket)
systems.warhead_notes: 45 kg HE warhead (CSIS); 240mm caliber, 407 kg launch weight.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: 2006 Lebanon War (Fajr-class rockets struck the Haifa area)
systems.salvo_notes: Part of Hezbollah's 100+/day deep-strike fire in 2006; the Fajr tier sits between Katyushas and Zelzal-class heavy rockets in Hezbollah's range ladder.
systems.notes: Iran began transferring Fajr-3/Fajr-5 to Hezbollah in the early 2000s — the first rockets that put Haifa within reach from southern Lebanon.

systems.name: Falaq-1 / Falaq-2
systems.origin: Iran (240mm Falaq-1, 333mm Falaq-2)
systems.warhead_notes: Falaq-1: ~50 kg HE; Falaq-2: 120 kg improved warhead per CSIS — heavy blast effect at short range.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Heavy documented use from late 2023 in the border war; first claimed Falaq-2 combat launch August 2024
systems.salvo_notes: Near-daily Falaq-1 strikes on border positions and towns like Kiryat Shmona during Oct 2023 – Nov 2024; Hezbollah publicized its first Falaq-2 launches in August 2024.
systems.notes: Hezbollah's preferred heavy hammer for the first kilometers over the border — big warheads on short-flight rockets that give defenses minimal engagement time.

systems.name: Burkan
systems.origin: Hezbollah/Syrian-developed IRAM-type heavy rocket (Syrian civil-war lineage)
systems.warhead_notes: Oversized HE warhead of 100-500 kg on a short-range rocket body; destruction radius up to ~150 m (Alma Center).
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Late 2023 (border war)
systems.salvo_notes: Used repeatedly in multi-rocket strikes on IDF border posts through 2024; footage of Burkan impacts became a Hezbollah propaganda staple.
systems.notes: A weapon born of Syria's siege warfare adopted against Israeli border fortifications — trades range for one of the heaviest warheads of any rocket fired at Israel.

systems.name: Zelzal-2
systems.origin: Iran (610mm unguided heavy rocket, delivered via Syria from the early 2000s)
systems.warhead_notes: 600 kg HE warhead (CSIS); unguided, so useful mainly against city-sized targets or as feedstock for guidance conversion.
systems.guidance: unguided (spin-stabilized); Iranian kits convert it into a Fateh-110-class guided missile
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Not documented as fired — held as a strategic stockpile (Israel destroyed Zelzal launchers on the ground in the 2006 war's opening strikes)
systems.salvo_notes: No documented salvo use; Iranian suitcase-sized kits reportedly convert a Zelzal-2 into a ~300 km guided missile in 2-3 hours at $5,000-$10,000 per conversion (BICOM).
systems.notes: The heart of Hezbollah's 'precision project': from 2016 Iran smuggled GPS-guidance conversion kits for Zelzal-2s — a program Israel repeatedly bombed.

systems.name: Fateh-110 / M-600
systems.origin: Iran (Fateh-110, a guided evolution of the Zelzal-2); Syria produced the M-600 copy transferred to Hezbollah around 2010
systems.warhead_notes: 450-500 kg HE; the Qader-1 fired at Tel Aviv carried a 500 kg warhead. Precision-guided versions are the core of Hezbollah's PGM project — CEPs from ~500 m down to tens of meters claimed.
systems.guidance: inertial + satellite (GPS-aided); quasi-ballistic with maneuvering variants
systems.speed: Short-range ballistic missile, roughly Mach 3-4 terminal (reported)
systems.first_used_vs_israel: September 25, 2024 — Hezbollah's first-ever ballistic missile launch at Tel Aviv (intercepted by David's Sling)
systems.salvo_notes: Single-missile use documented (Sept 25, 2024). Israeli intelligence assessed Hezbollah held hundreds of Fateh-110/M-600-class missiles; most were targeted in the Sept–Nov 2024 air campaign.
systems.notes: The most strategically watched item in Hezbollah's arsenal: a genuinely guided ballistic missile family, its lone combat use against Tel Aviv intercepted.

systems.name: Mirsad-1
systems.origin: Iran (HESA Ababil-2/Ababil-T family), operated by Hezbollah since the early 2000s
systems.warhead_notes: Up to ~40 kg of explosives in one-way attack configuration.
systems.speed: ~370 km/h, ceiling ~3,000 m; flies low to evade radar
systems.first_used_vs_israel: First penetrated Israeli airspace on reconnaissance in November 2004; used as an attack drone from October 2023
systems.salvo_notes: October 13, 2024: two Mirsads launched from Lebanon; one evaded detection and hit a Golani Brigade dining hall in Binyamina — 4 soldiers killed, ~60 wounded, the deadliest single Hezbollah drone strike of the war.
systems.notes: Hezbollah's drone campaign proved harder to detect than rockets — low, slow and small, several crossed 40+ km into Israel before interception or impact.

systems.name: Almas
systems.origin: Iran — reverse-engineered from Israeli Spike missiles captured by Hezbollah in the 2006 war
systems.warhead_notes: Tandem shaped-charge (anti-armor); Almas-1 ~4 km, Almas-2 ~8 km, Almas-3 up to 16 km from aerial platforms.
systems.guidance: electro-optical seeker with datalink — fire-and-observe, Spike-style lofted attack profile
systems.first_used_vs_israel: January 2024 (videoed strikes on border surveillance posts)
systems.salvo_notes: Used in repeated single-shot precision strikes on IDF observation posts, radars and even an Iron Dome battery area through 2024.
systems.notes: A bitter irony documented by Israeli media: an Israeli Spike cloned by Iran and fired back at Israeli border installations, giving Hezbollah true precision at the tactical edge.

systems.name: Palestine-2
systems.origin: Houthi-assembled with Iranian assistance; assessed as a clone/derivative of Iran's solid-fuel Kheibar Shekan-2 / Fattah lineage
systems.warhead_notes: ~500 kg claimed; two-stage solid fuel with a maneuvering re-entry vehicle. Houthi 'hypersonic' branding (claimed Mach 16) is treated with heavy skepticism by analysts — the Israeli Air Force said it has no evidence of a true hypersonic weapon.
systems.speed: Claimed Mach 16 (unverified); analysts assess Kheibar Shekan-class performance
systems.first_used_vs_israel: September 15, 2024 (first missile from Yemen to reach central Israel)
systems.salvo_notes: Fired singly, roughly weekly during peaks: 52 Houthi ballistic missiles + 13 drones at Israel between March 18 and June 28, 2025. May 4, 2025: one evaded THAAD and Arrow and hit Ben Gurion Airport's perimeter, injuring 6-8.
systems.notes: The Ben Gurion strike was the propaganda high-point of the Houthi campaign — a single missile that briefly halted international air traffic.

systems.name: Zulfiqar (Houthi)
systems.origin: Iranian-supplied Scud/Ghadr-lineage liquid-fuel missile, Houthi-modified
systems.warhead_notes: Scud/Ghadr-lineage HE warhead, ~500-650 kg class assessed. Reaching Eilat from northern Yemen requires ~1,600+ km, which led analysts to conclude a Ghadr-class missile was in play.
systems.speed: Ballistic; hypersonic on re-entry (as with any 1,200+ km-class BM)
systems.first_used_vs_israel: October 31, 2023 (first Houthi ballistic missile attack on Israel — intercepted by Arrow 2, Arrow's first combat kill)
systems.salvo_notes: Launched in small salvos of 1-3 missiles toward Eilat in Oct-Nov 2023 — all intercepted or fell short; the Oct 31 Arrow 2 engagement is cited as the first combat interception in space.
systems.notes: Analysis of the 2023 launches concluded the Houthis were using modified Scud-family missiles with ranges beyond anything they had fired before, confirming Iranian MRBM transfer to Yemen.

systems.name: Toofan
systems.origin: Assessed as practically identical to Iran's Ghadr-F (liquid-fuel Shahab-3 derivative), displayed by the Houthis in September 2023
systems.warhead_notes: Ghadr-class separating warhead ~650 kg; simulations found the 1,950 km claim plausible — enough to cover all of Israel from northern Yemen.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Paraded September 2023; linked to long-range Houthi launches at Israel from late 2023 onward
systems.salvo_notes: Single-missile launches typical of Houthi long-range strikes.
systems.notes: Together with Zulfiqar and the Palestine family, Toofan shows the Houthis fielding Iranian MRBM technology under local names — the first non-state actor to sustain 1,500+ km ballistic missile strikes.

systems.name: Quds cruise missile family
systems.origin: Iranian design (Soumar/Paveh '351' family per US DIA); assembled and operated by the Houthis
systems.warhead_notes: Warhead size undisclosed (Quds-1 total mass only ~450 kg, so a relatively small HE charge); Quds-1 ~700-800 km, Quds-2 ~1,350 km, Quds-4 claimed up to ~2,000 km.
systems.guidance: inertial + satellite navigation, low-altitude terrain-hugging profile
systems.first_used_vs_israel: October 19, 2023 (USS Carney intercepted 4 Houthi cruise missiles and 15 drones assessed as heading toward Israel)
systems.salvo_notes: Oct 19, 2023 salvo of 4 cruise missiles + 15 drones; later typically 1-2 missiles per launch at Eilat; one reached the Eilat area in March 2024.
systems.notes: The Quds family's low-altitude approach makes it a different detection problem from ballistic missiles and forced Israel to widen radar coverage over the Red Sea approach.

systems.name: Samad-3
systems.origin: Houthi-produced with Iranian design assistance (Samad family)
systems.warhead_notes: Explosive payload up to ~40 kg; extended-range conformal fuel tank, ~4.5 m wingspan, pusher prop.
systems.speed: Slow subsonic pusher-prop drone (~200 km/h class)
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Launch attempts from October 2023; July 19, 2024 a Samad-3 ('Yafa') struck central Tel Aviv
systems.salvo_notes: Typically single-drone sorties. July 19, 2024, 3:12 a.m.: one flew ~2,000 km, evaded detection and exploded near the US embassy branch in Tel Aviv, killing one man and injuring ten — the first fatal Houthi strike inside Israel.
systems.notes: The Tel Aviv hit exposed a gap in drone detection (the drone was tracked but not classified as hostile) and triggered Israel's first airstrike on Yemen the next day.

systems.name: Emad
systems.origin: Iran (liquid-fuel Shahab-3/Ghadr derivative with maneuverable re-entry vehicle, unveiled 2015)
systems.warhead_notes: ~750 kg HE with a finned, maneuverable re-entry vehicle; Iran claims CEP ~50 m — Iran's first 'precision' MRBM.
systems.guidance: inertial + satnav with terminally guided maneuvering re-entry vehicle
systems.speed: Liquid-fuel MRBM; hypersonic on re-entry (~2 km/s class descent)
systems.first_used_vs_israel: April 13-14, 2024 (Operation True Promise)
systems.salvo_notes: Fired in every direct Iranian attack: April 2024 (part of 120+ ballistic missiles), October 1, 2024 (~180-200 in ~30 minutes), June 2025 (bulk of ~550-590 missiles with Ghadr), and the 2026 war (~650 missiles total).
systems.notes: JINSA's July 2025 cost study put Emad at ~$250,000 per round — Iran's cheap workhorse for mass barrages; most were intercepted by Arrow, David's Sling and US THAAD/Aegis.

systems.name: Ghadr
systems.origin: Iran (improved Shahab-3, liquid fuel; basis for the Houthi Toofan and the Emad)
systems.warhead_notes: Warhead reduced from ~1,000 kg to ~650 kg across variants to buy range (Ghadr-S 1,350 km → Ghadr-F 1,950 km); conventional HE, separating warhead.
systems.salvo_notes: With Emad, formed the bulk of the October 1, 2024 (~200-missile) and June 2025 (~550-590-missile) barrages; also fired in the 2026 war. Cost estimates for Iranian missiles vary widely between analysts.
systems.notes: A 1990s-lineage design kept relevant by mass: Iran fired more Shahab-3-family (Ghadr/Emad) rounds at Israel in 2024-2026 than any other missile type.

systems.name: Kheibar Shekan
systems.origin: Iran, IRGC Aerospace Force (third-generation solid-fuel MRBM, unveiled 2022)
systems.warhead_notes: ~500-550 kg HE in a tri-conic maneuverable re-entry vehicle designed to evade terminal defenses; composite body, launch-ready solid fuel. Basis for the Houthi Palestine-2.
systems.guidance: inertial/satnav with terminal-phase maneuvering re-entry vehicle
systems.speed: Solid-fuel MRBM, 11.4 m / 6.3 t; impact-speed figures disagree between sources
systems.first_used_vs_israel: April 13-14, 2024 (debris identified); used at scale June 2025
systems.salvo_notes: One of the main types in Iran's June 2025 barrages; its compact size lets more be stored in underground 'missile cities', sustaining multi-wave salvos.
systems.notes: Several June 2025 impacts in Israeli cities were attributed to Kheibar Shekan-class missiles that leaked through saturated defenses.

systems.name: Fattah-1
systems.origin: Iran, IRGC (unveiled June 2023; billed as Iran's first 'hypersonic' missile)
systems.warhead_notes: Sources disagree: ~350-450 kg per some references, up to ~500 kg per others; two-stage solid fuel with a thrust-vector-controlled maneuvering warhead.
systems.guidance: inertial/satnav; maneuvering re-entry vehicle with claimed in-flight course correction
systems.speed: Claimed Mach 13-15 terminal; Western analysts class it as a maneuvering-RV ballistic missile rather than a true hypersonic glide vehicle
systems.first_used_vs_israel: Debris identified from both the April and October 2024 strikes; IRGC claimed mass use October 1, 2024
systems.salvo_notes: IRGC said Fattah-1s were among ~200 missiles fired Oct 1, 2024 (first claimed combat use of a 'hypersonic' weapon against Israel); used again in June 2025.
systems.notes: Iran's flagship prestige missile. Independent analysts confirmed its debris in Israel but dispute the 'unstoppable hypersonic' framing — Arrow and THAAD engaged Fattah-class re-entry vehicles with claimed success.

systems.name: Haj Qasem
systems.origin: Iran (solid-fuel, two-stage MRBM unveiled August 2020, named for Qasem Soleimani)
systems.warhead_notes: ~500 kg HE; 2024 upgrades reportedly added electro-optical terminal guidance and jamming resistance.
systems.guidance: inertial/satnav; maneuvering re-entry, reported electro-optical terminal seeker on upgraded rounds
systems.first_used_vs_israel: June 2025 (Twelve-Day War)
systems.salvo_notes: Named by Iran among the types fired in the June 2025 campaign; solid fuel allows quick multi-launcher salvos from dispersed sites.
systems.notes: Part of Iran's newer solid-fuel generation that launches with little warning — exactly the class Israel's February 2026 preemptive campaign prioritized destroying on the ground.

systems.name: Sejjil
systems.origin: Iran (first Iranian two-stage all-solid-fuel MRBM, flight-tested from 2008)
systems.warhead_notes: ~700 kg payload; 18 m, 23.6 t missile. Iran claimed a possible submunition payload on the June 2025 combat round.
systems.speed: Two-stage solid fuel; Iran claims Tel Aviv reachable in under 7 minutes from launch
systems.first_used_vs_israel: June 18, 2025 (first combat use ever; Israel said it was intercepted)
systems.salvo_notes: Single claimed launch during the Twelve-Day War — a demonstrative first combat use after 17 years in development.
systems.notes: Storable, quick-launch solid fuel makes Sejjil harder to preempt than the liquid-fuel Ghadr/Emad family; its one combat launch was widely read as an escalation signal.

systems.name: Shahed-131 / Shahed-136
systems.origin: Iran, Shahed Aviation Industries (delta-wing one-way attack drones)
systems.warhead_notes: Shahed-131: ~10-15 kg class; Shahed-136: 30-50 kg HE/fragmentation nose warhead, newer variants reported up to ~90 kg. Range estimates span 1,000-2,500 km for the 136.
systems.speed: Subsonic, ~185 km/h max (piston engine, pusher prop)
systems.first_used_vs_israel: April 13-14, 2024 (~170 launched directly by Iran; proxy Shahed-type launches toward Israel began October 2023)
systems.salvo_notes: April 13-14, 2024: ~170 one-way attack drones in one night — none reached Israeli territory (99% interception). June 2025: over 1,000 launched across the Twelve-Day War.
systems.notes: The defining cheap mass-attack weapon of the decade, commonly cited at $20k-$50k apiece. Its slow speed gives hours of warning from Iran — and Israel downed virtually all of them.

systems.name: Paveh
systems.origin: Iran (land-attack cruise missile unveiled February 2023, Soumar/Kh-55-lineage family)
systems.warhead_notes: Warhead weight undisclosed; terrain-following low-altitude profile for radar evasion.
systems.first_used_vs_israel: April 13-14, 2024 (30+ cruise missiles in the True Promise attack; none reached their targets)
systems.salvo_notes: April 2024: 30+ land-attack cruise missiles launched in one wave, downed largely by fighter aircraft; the same family serves Iraqi militias and the Houthis under other names.
systems.notes: Iran's export of the Paveh family to Iraq's militias and Yemen effectively ringed Israel with the same cruise missile under three different names.

actor_arsenal_estimates.estimate: ~20,000 rockets and mortar bombs on Oct 7, 2023 per Israeli estimates, most short-range. IDF one-year data: 13,200 projectiles fired from Gaza (≈5,000 on Oct 7 alone). Arsenal and production largely destroyed or depleted through 2024-25; fire fell to sporadic single launches and essentially stopped after the October 2025 Gaza ceasefire.

Pre-Oct 2023: 120,000-200,000 rockets and missiles commonly cited (CSIS ~130,000; Israeli official estimate 150,000). IDF assessed 70-80% destroyed by the Nov 27, 2024 ceasefire. Early 2026: ~20,000-25,000 remaining; after the March-April 2026 Lebanon war, roughly 10,000-23,000 left, mostly short-range — still enough for 200-rocket barrage days.

Total inventory not publicly quantified; capability is Iranian-resupplied. Launch record vs Israel: 200+ ballistic/cruise missiles and drones in the first 14 months; 52 ballistic missiles + 13 drones between Mar 18 and Jun 28, 2025; attacks paused after the Oct 2025 Gaza ceasefire and resumed Mar 28, 2026 for the Iran war.

~2,500-3,000 ballistic missiles pre-June 2025 (US/Israeli estimates), of which ~2,000-2,500 could reach Israel. Fired ~550-590 at Israel in the June 2025 Twelve-Day War. Rebuilt toward ~2,500 Israel-range missiles by early 2026, then fired ~650 in the Feb-Apr 2026 war; an Israeli Air Force official estimated just over 1,000 remaining at the April 2026 ceasefire, with 300+ launchers destroyed cutting fire rates by 70-92%.

defenses.name: Iron Dome
defenses.intercepts: Short-range rockets, mortar bombs, and drones (threat ranges roughly 4-70 km); selective engagement — only shoots at projectiles headed for populated areas
defenses.record: ~90%+ claimed interception rate since 2011, with 10,000+ combat intercepts by its 15th anniversary in April 2026; independent analysts estimate 80-90%, lower under saturation barrages.

defenses.name: David's Sling
defenses.intercepts: Heavy rockets, short-range ballistic missiles, cruise missiles and aircraft in the 40-300 km band — between Iron Dome and Arrow
defenses.record: First operational intercepts May 2023 (Gaza heavy rockets); intercepted Hezbollah's Qader-1 ballistic missile over Tel Aviv on Sept 25, 2024; engaged Iranian missiles 2024-2026.

defenses.name: Arrow 2
defenses.intercepts: Ballistic missiles in the upper atmosphere / edge of space (terminal-phase)
defenses.record: First-ever combat intercept Oct 31, 2023 against a Houthi ballistic missile ~100 km up — described as the first combat interception in space; Arrow-family rates above 90% reported.

defenses.name: Arrow 3
defenses.intercepts: Medium/long-range ballistic missiles exoatmospherically (hit-to-kill in space) — Israel's top layer against Iranian MRBMs
defenses.record: First combat intercept Nov 9, 2023 (Houthi missile bound for Eilat); primary killer of Iranian MRBMs in the 2024, 2025 and 2026 barrages. Interceptor stocks ran low in June 2025, prompting a 2026 US-Israel co-production push.

defenses.name: THAAD (US Army)
defenses.intercepts: Medium/intermediate-range ballistic missiles in terminal high-altitude phase; US battery deployed to Israel October 2024
defenses.record: First-ever THAAD combat intercept Dec 27, 2024 vs a Houthi missile; at least six Houthi missiles downed by mid-2025; shared a publicized miss (with Arrow) on the May 4, 2025 Ben Gurion strike; heavily expended in the June 2025 war.

defenses.name: C-Dome
defenses.intercepts: Naval Iron Dome on Sa'ar 6 corvettes — rockets, cruise missiles and drones approaching from the sea
defenses.record: First operational combat interception April 9, 2024 (hostile UAV approaching Eilat); protected the Eilat/Red Sea approach from Houthi drones and cruise missiles thereafter.

defenses.name: Iron Beam
defenses.intercepts: Rockets, mortars and drones at short range using a ~100 kW-class high-power laser — unlimited magazine, complement to Iron Dome
defenses.record: First operational system delivered to the Israeli Air Force Dec 28, 2025 — the world's first fielded high-power laser air-defense system; cost per shot cited at ~$2-5 of electricity vs $40k-100k per Iron Dome interceptor.

notable_events.event: Hamas-led assault opens with the largest rocket barrage ever fired at Israel: 2,200-5,000 rockets and mortar bombs in the opening ~20-30 minutes. IDF one-year totals: 26,000+ projectiles from all fronts — 13,200 from Gaza, 12,400 from Lebanon, ~400 from Iran, 180 from Yemen, 60 from Syria.
First Houthi ballistic missile attack on Israel; Arrow 2 records its first-ever combat interception, engaging outside the atmosphere.

Iran's first-ever direct attack on Israel: ~170 Shahed drones, 30+ cruise missiles, 120+ ballistic missiles overnight. US-led coalition and Israel intercept ~99%; ~5 ballistic missiles hit Nevatim airbase.
Houthi Samad-3 drone flies ~2,000 km and strikes central Tel Aviv, killing one — the first fatal Houthi strike in Israel; Israel strikes Hodeidah, Yemen the next day.
Hezbollah fires its first-ever ballistic missile at Tel Aviv — a Qader-1 aimed at Mossad HQ — intercepted by David's Sling.
Iran launches ~180-200 ballistic missiles in ~30 minutes — the largest single ballistic missile salvo in history. Most intercepted; ~20-32 impacts at Nevatim airbase.
Hezbollah Mirsad-1 drone evades detection and hits a Golani Brigade base dining hall in Binyamina: 4 soldiers killed, ~60 wounded — the deadliest drone strike of the war.
Hezbollah fires ~250 rockets and projectiles in one day — its heaviest barrage of the war — three days before the Nov 27 ceasefire.
First-ever combat intercept by a THAAD battery anywhere: the US Army system in Israel downs a Houthi medium-range ballistic missile.
A Houthi ballistic missile (claimed Palestine-2) evades both THAAD and Arrow and hits the perimeter of Ben Gurion Airport, injuring 6-8 and halting international flights for days.

Twelve-Day War: Iran fires ~550-591 ballistic missiles and 1,000+ drones at Israel. ~86-90% intercepted; 59-64 missile impacts kill ~30 and wound ~2,000. First combat Sejjil launch and cluster-submunition warheads documented June 18-19.
Gaza war ceasefire takes effect; rocket fire from Gaza has dwindled to sporadic launches, and Houthi attacks pause following the deal.
The 2026 Iran war begins: ~900 US-Israeli strikes in 12 hours; Iran retaliates with the heaviest missile-and-drone barrages ever fired at Israel — 10,162 alerts in a single day.
